qa_pairs.question: How do you run a new Abaqus Standard Analysis job for version 2026 or newer on a single node within a project directory on an Alliance cluster?
qa_pairs.answer: For Abaqus version 2026 or newer, a Slurm script would include `module load abaqus/2026` and execute the command `abaqus job=testsp1 input=mystd-sim.inp scratch=$SLURM_TMPDIR cpus=$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE interactive mp_mode=threads memory="$((${SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE}-3072))MB"`. Optionally, one can uncomment `#gpus=$SLURM_GPUS_ON_NODE` to utilize a GPU. The Slurm script also defines resources such as `--account`, `--time`, `--cpus-per-task` (e.g., 4), `--mem` (e.g., 8G), and `--nodes=1`.

qa_pairs.question: What is the correct syntax to specify restart data in an Abaqus input file for Standard Analysis jobs?
qa_pairs.answer: To write restart data every N=12 time increments, specify `*RESTART, WRITE, OVERLAY, FREQUENCY=12` in the input file. Alternatively, to write restart data for a total of 12 time increments, specify `*RESTART, WRITE, OVERLAY, NUMBER INTERVAL=12, TIME MARKS=NO`.

qa_pairs.question: How does one restart a previously run Abaqus Standard Analysis job on a single node using a project directory script?
qa_pairs.answer: To restart a Standard Analysis job, a Slurm script for Abaqus 2026 or newer would execute the command `abaqus job=testsp2 oldjob=testsp1 input=mystd-sim-restart.inp scratch=$SLURM_TMPDIR cpus=$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE interactive mp_mode=threads memory="$((${SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE}-3072))MB"`. The restart input file (`mystd-sim-restart.inp`) must contain the lines `*HEADING` and `*RESTART, READ`.
